title: Traffic safety adjudicator and rollback scorer for gradual upgrades
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: implement a Traffic Safety Adjudicator (TSA) service that converts telemetry and eval signals into deterministic gate decisions and a numeric rollback score. TSA will be used by the rollout controller to: 1) automatically pause or abort ramps, 2) trigger automatic rollbacks when score exceeds thresholds, and 3) produce audit logs for postmortems.

Scope: build the adjudication rules engine, wire in Console metric streams (latency P95/P99, 5xx/error rate, token cost anomaly, hallucination/regression indicators from prompt-eval), integrate with feature flag evaluation (LaunchDarkly) for cohort selection, and expose a decision API for the rollout orchestrator.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- TSA produces a per-cohort decision (GO/PAUSE/ROLLBACK) and a rollback_score (0-100) every 30s for active canaries.
- Rollback_score is deterministic from inputs and rule versions; adjudications persisted to audit log and visible in Console.
- Rollout controller consumes TSA decisions and honors auto-pause/auto-rollback policies configurable per-release.
- Integration tests simulate injected latency/error spikes and validate automated pause/rollback behavior.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Rule approach: prioritized deterministic ruleset (thresholds + hysteresis) instead of ML-based classifier to keep behavior auditable for compliance. We will version rule sets and store them in release manifests for reproducibility.
- Signals: start with latency P95, request error rate, and embedding similarity regressions from evals; add hallucination signal later once we have a stable detector.
- Scoring: rollback_score is a weighted sum of normalized signals (weights per-signal configurable via release policy). We keep default weights conservative to avoid false positives at low traffic.
- Cohorts: prefer tenant-aware cohorts (top-20% traffic, internal tests, canary users) to avoid small-sample noise.
- Timing: 30s adjudication window balances responsiveness and noisy metric variance; future work may add dynamic window sizing.

Implementation plan:
1) Rule engine prototype (library) + unit tests (Feb week 4).
2) Decision API + persistence schema in Console (Mar week 1).
3) Integration with rollout controller and feature flags (Mar week 2).
4) Canary experiments on staging -> production shadow -> limited production roll (Mar week 3).

Monitoring & playbook:
- Dashboard: per-cohort time series of signals, rollback_score, and decision. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/TS-51327 (placeholder).
- Alerts: PagerDuty on auto-rollback OR if TSA API error rate > 1% over 5m.
- Runbook: explicit manual override steps, immediate revert PR links, and SRE contact list included in Confluence playbook. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/TS-51327+playbook (placeholder).

Testing:
- Unit tests for scoring math and hysteresis handling.
- Integration test that injects 50% error rate and ensures rollback_score > threshold and orchestrator triggers rollback.
- Chaos experiment scheduled with Chaos Team to validate guardrails (Apr cycle).

Open questions:
- Exact default weights for hallucination vs latency (PM to decide after eval quality review).
- Whether to allow per-tenant overrides for rollback sensitivity (security/compliance trade-offs).

Next steps:
- Finalize rule schema and default weights (owner: PM - Lena Park).
- Create initial Console dashboard stub and test stream wiring (owner: Eng - Evan Morales).
- Security review kickoff with Compliance (owner: Security - Marcus Chen).
